eligibilityPolicy.knownConsequence: v4's labeled sample excludes all 22 known-terminated KR securities' observations entirely, at every signal date, under current evidence. This is NOT the same defect alpha-opportunity-model-v3 found in the US leg (NO_TERMINATED_SECURITY_IN_SAMPLE, where the panel never priced a departed name at all, so termination was structurally invisible): here the 22 names ARE priced, ARE members of the PIT KR universe on their live dates, and DO still enter feature computation and cross-sectional context -- only their own forward-return LABEL is withheld, for a disclosed, quantified, bounded and shrinking fraction of member-dates (alphaOpportunityV3SurvivorshipAudit: 3.7366% of tradable KR member-dates, 7.93% in 2013 declining to 0.76% in 2025). It is still a real, disclosed survivorship-conditioning limitation: v4's labeled sample never observes the realised forward outcome of a name that is about to be delisted or merged out, which understates tail risk relative to the true investable universe. `requiredDiagnostics.exclusionsClusterAroundTerminalEventsCheck` in evaluationPreregistration requires the future execution to publish this quantitatively rather than let it pass unremarked, and evaluationPreregistration's own verdict vocabulary must be read alongside this caveat, never as an unconditional statement about KR delisting risk.
neverAllowed: treating an unresolved exchange ratio or successor as final
carrying the last traded price forward through a termination
inventing an ex-date from a record date or any other computed rule
assuming zero recovery for an unresolved termination
excluding or including an observation based on its realised return magnitude
using today's KR universe membership as a historical one
a new exclusion rule invented after an outcome is seen
eligibilityPolicy.rule: A security not in the 22 is unaffected: ordinary production/replay mechanics (MISSING_FORWARD_PRICE_OR_DELISTING) apply unchanged. For one of the 22: `exDateSemanticsResolved` must read READY in the sealed completeness matrix before ANY observation on that security -- pre- or post-termination -- is eligible, because the security's entire trading life is on a price-return basis (Yahoo serves no distributions for a delisted KR ticker) while the matched benchmark and every continuing name are total-return; this is not only a terminal-window problem. A window whose exit session is after the security's last traded session additionally requires `terminationTypeResolved`, `terminalConsiderationResolved`, `successorResolvedWhereRequired` (where applicable) and `terminalActionChainResolved` all READY, and -- where a successor is required -- that successor's own price panel.

evaluationPreregistration.A_absoluteCalibration: date-balanced pooled realised = a + b * predicted net relative return (not within-date demeaned); b lower > 0; a and b intervals published; MSE improvement over training mean lower > 0
evaluationPreregistration.B_ordering: equal-date rank IC lower > 0; within-date slope lower > 0
evaluationPreregistration.C_probability: Brier and log-loss improvement over training prevalence (net label) lower > 0; pooled date-balanced ECE upper <= 0.05 (v2 simulated null recorded in v2 spec)
evaluationPreregistration.D_disclosedBesideNotGating: D recomputed separately for EXPECTATION_POSITIVE_OUTPERFORM_PROBABILITY_NOT_ABOVE_HALF and FITTED_INTERVAL_SPANS_OUTSIDE_OPTION subsets, descriptive only
evaluationPreregistration.D_positiveExpectedAlphaRegion: on dates with >= 1 POSITIVE_EXPECTED_ALPHA name: date-mean realised net relative return of those names lower > 0 (the outside-option test) AND same-date spread over non-positive names lower > 0 (lesser of level and spread); plus, disclosed not gated, realised-on-predicted slope inside the positive region and realised means by within-date terciles of predicted expectedNetAlpha among positive names (terciles fixed from predictions alone); no predicted-alpha threshold other than 0 is ever evaluated
evaluationPreregistration.E_stability: annual folds >= 70% jointly positive (rank IC, Brier, MSE); D point estimate positive in each chronological half; no subgroup beyond the two horizons
evaluationPreregistration.F_missingnessIntegrity: before ANY gate in A-E may be interpreted, the execution report MUST publish every field in `requiredDiagnostics` below; a report missing one is not a partial result, it is DATA_INSUFFICIENT for every claim
evaluationPreregistration.dependence: moving blocks of 26 whole weekly dates, 2000 draws, seed 42, Bonferroni across the two horizon claims (21D, 126D): twoSidedTail=0.0125, 97.5% two-sided intervals
evaluationPreregistration.status: PREREGISTERED_BEFORE_ANY_OUTCOME; not executable in this PR

newInteractions.rationale: Section 11 of this study's own governing task requires any interaction to be selected on economic mechanism, PIT availability, adequate historical coverage and manageable multiplicity -- never on outcome data. Every candidate hypothesis that needs investor flow (candidate 5, flow confirmation x price/attention) is excluded above as access-unproven. The remaining candidates (fundamental state/change x liquidity shock; price leadership x liquidity persistence; weak fundamentals x liquidity shock; attention x price-leadership divergence) all involve the same small, already-carried-forward KR feature set (relative126, acceleration21, vol63, logVolumeShock60, shockPersistence5d, volumePriceAlignment, and three DART accounting fields dark before 2015) that v1-v3 never found PIT-unsafe but also never tested in combination. Rather than add an untested interaction term to a preregistration whose purpose is closing a DATA-INTEGRITY gap, v4 carries v3's linear/shallow-HGB-complement model family unchanged, which already lets the shallow HGB complement (never a decision, per carriedFromV3.models.interpretation) surface any such interaction as complementary evidence without this spec committing to one by name. A dedicated interaction study, if warranted, is a separate preregistration.

scope.conservativeBaseline: a conservative baseline model over v3's already-vetted KR feature set and model family; not a test of any new interaction (see newInteractions) and not a re-tune of alpha-reliability-v1's closed calibration or alpha-risk-separation-v1's closed sleeve questions; its failure or blockage says nothing about those
scope.regions: KR-only. US carries a separate, structurally different survivorship defect (NO_TERMINATED_SECURITY_IN_SAMPLE: the panel never priced 212 of 324 departed S&P 500 identities at all, so termination is invisible, not merely basis-inconsistent) that this PR does not touch, repair, or wait for. Region symmetry is not a reason to hold KR back: alpha-research-philosophy-v2 section 1 already states 'treating US and KR as one model, or as two models forever' is not required, and regional-alpha-research-separation-v1 already separated the two before this PR existed.
